title: Physical Superintelligence says a non-public Anthropic model proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture
subtitle: The 2008 question about quantum speedups has a Lean-formalized proof — if peer review holds, it's the strongest AI-assisted theoretical computer science result so far.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) announced on November 6 that an internal research system, running a non-public Anthropic model, produced a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis posed the question in 2008: on random inputs, can quantum computers deliver more than a polynomial speedup over classical computers? PSI's result, led by technical staff member David Turturean, says the answer is no — quantum advantage on average-case inputs is at most polynomial. The manuscript and a Lean 4 formalization are both public on PSI's site.

The Lean formalization is the key artifact. Lean is a proof assistant that mechanically verifies every logical step, so once the formal statement matches the informal conjecture, the proof itself is machine-checked. What is not yet checked is whether the formalized statement is a faithful translation of what Aaronson and Ambainis actually conjectured — that remains a human judgment call, and neither Aaronson nor Ambainis has issued a public assessment. There is also no peer review yet.

If the result holds up, it's the most substantive AI-assisted theoretical computer science claim to date. OpenAI announced proofs of smaller conjectures in October, and Anthropic's Claude has been credited with bounds on the Riemann zeta function and Fermat's Last Theorem formalization. A full resolution of a long-open quantum complexity question would be a different tier — and notable that the model powering it is not publicly available, which raises the familiar frontier-capability transparency question.

A takeaway for learners: AI-assisted mathematics is becoming a distinct research skill. The useful question is no longer 'can a model prove theorems' but 'what is the human researcher's role in the pipeline' — framing the problem, auditing the Lean statement, checking that the formal version matches what was asked. Those judgment steps are now the bottleneck, and they are learnable. Start reading proof-assistant-based papers now; the vocabulary will matter.
